paper.title: Volunteering as Red Queen mechanism for cooperation in public goods games

headline: Hauert 2002 Optional Public Goods (agent-based): 3/3 locked clauses REPRO; voluntary r=3 time-avg (C,D,L)=(0.29,0.35,0.36) vs compulsory coop=0.00; loner-dominated at r=1.8 (loner=1.00)

verdicts.gate: P1 RPS coexistence (r=3, sigma=1): each of C/D/L time-avg in (0.05, 0.90) AND cooperator amplitude > 0.10
P2 voluntary participation prevents all-D collapse: compulsory coop < 0.05, voluntary coop >= 0.15 AND exceeds compulsory by >= 0.10
P3 regime flip across r=2: at r=1.8,sigma=0.5 loner-dominated (loner > 0.5, coop < 0.15); at r=3,sigma=1 cooperation persists (coop >= 0.15)

extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published synthetic model; no real-world data; the contribution is whether the harness + locked-prediction discipline reproduce the loner-induced RPS coexistence, isolate voluntary participation as the rescue of cooperation, and would catch an artifact

citations: Hauert, C., De Monte, S., Hofbauer, J. & Sigmund, K. (2002). Volunteering as Red Queen mechanism for cooperation in public goods games. Science 296:1129-1132. doi:10.1126/science.1070582.

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction graded against the time-averaged strategy frequencies + cooperator amplitude
